items.verifier_note: The discharge summary and the 10-08 PCP note support the 9/29 ED visit for chest pain, the 3-day admission, the negative cardiac workup, no new medications, and the return to baseline per spouse.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions.
Falls and near-falls since last review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred after furosemide was started on 2026-10-08 (orthostasis or nocturia risk).

Furosemide start (2026-10-08) for lower-extremity edema and weight gain: review the indication documentation, follow-up electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium), renal function (creatinine/eGFR), and whether a repeat BMP was ordered and completed.

Weight trend across the window, with attention to the gain that prompted furosemide: compare to baseline and prior review, and flag any gain of about 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week, or sustained gain, for clinician review. Note BMI 30+ baseline.
Edema and cardiopulmonary symptoms: documented edema grade, dyspnea, orthopnea, chest pain or angina episodes, and use of PRN nitroglycerin spray since last review, including any frequency increase.

Blood pressure and heart rate trend (metoprolol succinate 100 mg, furosemide added): check for hypotension, orthostatic readings, bradycardia, and whether any dose change or hold parameters were documented.

Medication reconciliation: confirm the five active medications (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, furosemide, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) against pharmacy fills and the MAR; check for any starts or stops not reflected in the list, and any missed or late refills, especially clopidogrel and simvastatin.
Bleeding and antiplatelet safety: any bleeding, bruising, GI symptoms, or falls on clopidogrel; note that the allergy list is empty and confirm it was verified.
Lipid and cardiac follow-up items due: last lipid panel date, cardiology or primary care visits, and any ischemic heart disease care-plan items coming due before 2026-11-30.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screen status, depression screen and attendance at PACE programming (adult day, therapy, transport), plus caregiver strain or changes in living situation, and whether the care plan was updated to reflect the new edema/diuretic need.
